userStories.title: Record the targeted note revision in local proposal forgets
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Bind each new local proposal forget to the held note's id when available, while retaining legacy record compatibility.

**Motivation** — Project A proposed forgetting a user note. Project B then refiled it with the body "Use French". Running `nax memory approve` in A deleted B's replacement.

**Approach** — Implement these Target design requirements, not the baseline behavior:

- `MemoryPendingForget` (`packages/nax-agent/src/memory/types.ts`) and `PendingForgetSchema` (`records.ts`).
  - Target: the type and schema gain an optional `noteId?: string`. It holds the `id` of the note the mirror held when the forget was recorded. A line without the field still parses, and the field is omitted when the mirror held no note.
  - Why `id` and not `updatedAt`: `stagedNote` (`operations.ts`) gives every save, direct or proposal, a fresh `randomUUID()` id. `inForce` (approval of a pending save) restamps `updatedAt` but keeps `id`. So approving the same pending note from another project restamps it without making the forget stale, while a refile always does.
- `forget` in `createLocalMemoryProvider` (`packages/nax-agent/src/memory/local-provider.ts`).
  - Target: a proposal forget reads `store.readNote(request.scope, request.slug)` before rewriting the record. The queued entry carries `noteId: note.id` when that note is non-null. When `readNote` throws (for example `MEMORY_SCOPE_UNAVAILABLE` for a user forget on a store with no user directory), the entry is recorded without `noteId`, exactly as today. A direct forget is unchanged.
  - `sameEntries` also compares `noteId`, so a re-forget that names a new revision rewrites the record.
- New export `isStaleForget(entry: MemoryPendingForget, note: MemoryNote | null): boolean` in a new file `packages/nax-agent/src/memory/forget-revision.ts`. It returns `true` exactly when `entry.noteId` is a string, `note` is non-null, and `note.id !== entry.noteId`. In every other case it returns `false`: a legacy entry with no field, or a null note.

Modify `types.ts`, `records.ts` and `local-provider.ts`; create the helper and its unit tests. Preserve throughStore error mapping for mutations and record writes; only the added note lookup is best-effort. In `local-provider-pending-forgets.test.ts`, an exact assertion for a held target now includes noteId equal to that note's id; assertions for absent targets keep their four-field shape. In `store-pending-forgets.test.ts`, a line with or without noteId round-trips unchanged. Exercise a re-forget with unchanged request fields but a different held note id so the test detects omission of noteId from sameEntries.

**Scope** — In: optional revision persistence, best-effort lookup, revision-aware equality, shared predicate, and associated parsing/provider regressions. Out: stale-entry approval/index routing belongs to US-002; ACP registry and turn changes belong to US-003/US-004. Moving the pending-forget record of user-scope notes into the user directory is not done; the forget stays bound to the project that recorded it, and the revision check is the fix. A recorded forget written before this feature carries no revision and keeps the old behaviour; existing `pending-forgets.jsonl` files are not migrated. Remote memory providers are unchanged; only the local provider writes `pending-forgets.jsonl`, and a pull that rewrites a note's `id` from a remote provider is not reconciled with a recorded forget.

**Interface** — `noteId?: string` on `MemoryPendingForget` and its persisted schema; module export:
```typescript
export function isStaleForget(entry: MemoryPendingForget, note: MemoryNote | null): boolean
```
The helper is exported from its module for US-002, without requiring a new root-package public export. The existing store interface remains unchanged:
```typescript
readNote(scope: MemoryScope, slug: string): Promise<MemoryNote | null>;
```
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] isStaleForget returns true for an entry with noteId: "note-a" and a note whose id is "note-b".
[unit] isStaleForget returns false when the entry's noteId equals the note's id, even when the note's updatedAt has changed.
[unit] isStaleForget returns false for an entry with no noteId field, whatever the note's id.
[unit] isStaleForget returns false when the note is null.
[unit] parsePendingForgetLine parses a line carrying noteId into an entry whose noteId equals the line's value.
[unit] (control) parsePendingForgetLine parses a line without noteId into an entry with no noteId field.
[unit] When a proposal forget is pushed to createLocalMemoryProvider for a held user note with id "note-a", readPendingForgets() returns the entry with noteId equal to "note-a".
[unit] (control) When a proposal forget targets a slug the store holds no note for, readPendingForgets() returns an entry with no noteId field.
[unit] (control) When a proposal forget targets a user-scope slug on a store created with userDir: null, readPendingForgets() returns its entry without noteId instead of the push rejecting.
[unit] When a second proposal forget targets the same key after the note was refiled with a new id, readPendingForgets() returns a single entry for that key carrying the new id as noteId.
[unit] (control) When readNote throws during a proposal forget's revision lookup, the provider records the entry without noteId, exactly as today.

routing.reasoning: Additive optional persistence field and a small pure helper across four source modules using existing patterns; demonstrate new parsing/provider regressions failing before implementation, retaining legacy controls.

modifiedFiles.reason: the assertion that saves a note and then proposal-forgets it pins the recorded entry to exactly `{ clientId, scope, slug, reason }`; the entry now also carries `noteId`. The invariant becomes: those four fields as before, plus `noteId` equal to the held note's `id`. Assertions on forgets of a slug the store holds no note for keep the four-field shape unchanged.
a round-trip assertion that pins the exact parsed entry shape may need the optional `noteId`. The invariant becomes: a line with or without `noteId` round-trips unchanged.

userStories.title: Preserve refiled user notes when approving stale forgets
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Route approval and index refresh through the revision check so an old project-local forget cannot retire or mark a replacement shared user note.

**Motivation** — User notes are shared across projects, but the forget record is kept per project, so B's save never reached A's record.

**Approach** — Implement these Target design requirements, not the baseline behavior:

- `approveLocked` / `holdsRecordedForget` / `retireRecorded` (`packages/nax-agent/src/memory/operations.ts`).
  - Target: approval finds the recorded entry for the key. If `isStaleForget(entry, note)` is true, it removes that entry from the record (re-read after removal, the same way `retireRecorded` does, so another writer's entry survives) and calls `refreshIndex`. Approval then continues as if no forget were recorded: an active note comes back unchanged, and a pending note is put in force. A non-stale entry still retires the note as today. `operations.ts` is at 425 lines, so the new helper lives in `forget-revision.ts`.
- `markedForgets` (`packages/nax-agent/src/memory/index-render.ts`).
  - Target: a recorded entry is marked only when `isStaleForget(entry, await store.readNote(entry.scope, entry.slug))` is false. When that `readNote` throws (no user directory, or a path outside the scope root), the entry counts as not stale and is marked, as today. The record is not rewritten here. Held and source keys are unchanged.

Use the US-001 module export `isStaleForget(entry: MemoryPendingForget, note: MemoryNote | null): boolean`: it returns `true` exactly when `entry.noteId` is a string, `note` is non-null, and `note.id !== entry.noteId`. Preserve approval ordering under `orderedByMirrorLocks` + `withMirrorLock`; absent or retired notes are refused before the revision check. Failure handling: A recorded forget from before this feature (no `noteId`) is treated as current. Approval retires the note as before. The note is gone or retired when approval runs: `MEMORY_NOTE_NOT_FOUND`, as today. The revision check is never reached. Removing a stale entry from the record throws: The error propagates. The note is not deleted, and the stale entry stays, so the next approval finds it stale again.

Create `operations-approve-stale-forget.test.ts` by extending the existing single-store endToEnd(dir) pattern to two stores created with createMemoryStore over one shared userDir and separate project directories A and B. Give each its own `{ store, outbox: createMemoryOutbox({ dir: store.paths.outboxDir }), provider: createLocalMemoryProvider(store), logger }` for production operations, in proposal mode unless a case says otherwise. Baseline fixture: A saves user/lang with body `Use English` in direct mode, then records a proposal forget through forgetMemoryNote. B's refile means B saves user/lang with body `Use French` in proposal mode, minting a new id. Test direct refile separately, preserving its updatedAt on approval. Test B approving A's pending initial save without refile separately: the id stays the same and A's forget remains current. Drive approveMemoryNote and refreshMemoryIndex, and inspect the shared user index for the lang marker; predicate-only tests cannot prove production routing. Existing legacy approval/index assertions do not need modification.

**Scope** — In: stale-record removal and refresh, ordinary approval of the current note, stale-marker filtering, failure propagation, cross-project regression fixture. Out: record-field/provider/helper creation belongs to US-001; ACP changes belong to US-003/US-004. Moving the pending-forget record of user-scope notes into the user directory is not done; the forget stays bound to the project that recorded it, and the revision check is the fix. A recorded forget written before this feature carries no revision and keeps the old behaviour; existing `pending-forgets.jsonl` files are not migrated. Remote memory providers are unchanged; only the local provider writes `pending-forgets.jsonl`, and a pull that rewrites a note's `id` from a remote provider is not reconciled with a recorded forget.

**Interface** — Consume the upstream helper:
```typescript
export function isStaleForget(entry: MemoryPendingForget, note: MemoryNote | null): boolean
```
Integration entry: `approveMemoryNote(input)` runs `approveLocked` under `orderedByMirrorLocks` + `withMirrorLock`. Existing store operations remain unchanged:
```typescript
readNote(scope: MemoryScope, slug: string): Promise<MemoryNote | null>;
readPendingForgets(): Promise<MemoryPendingForget[]>;
writePendingForgets(entries: readonly MemoryPendingForget[]): Promise<void>;
```
The CLI approve message remains unchanged: a deleted note prints `forgot <scope>/<slug> (forget approved)`, an active one `<scope>/<slug> is already active; nothing to approve`, and otherwise `approved <scope>/<slug>`.
acceptanceCriteria: [integration] Given the two-store fixture and B's proposal refile of user/lang to Use French, approveMemoryNote on store A returns a note whose status is active, and its body is Use French.
[integration] After store A approves following B's proposal refile, store B's readNote("user", "lang") returns a note with status active.
[integration] (control) After that approval, store A's readPendingForgets() holds no entry for user/lang.
[integration] When B's refile is made in direct mode instead, approveMemoryNote on store A returns a note with status active.
[integration] When B's refile is made in direct mode instead, approveMemoryNote on store A returns a note whose updatedAt equals B's save.
[integration] (control) When store A's initial save of lang is in proposal mode and store B approves that pending note without a refile, a later approveMemoryNote on store A returns status deleted.
[integration] (control) When nothing changed lang after A recorded the forget, approveMemoryNote on store A returns status deleted.
[integration] (control) When a record line for user/lang with no noteId is written directly with writePendingForgets before B's refile, approveMemoryNote on store A still returns status deleted.

[integration] When store A is wrapped in a store whose writePendingForgets throws, approval after B's refile rejects with that error, and after that failed approval, readNote("user", "lang") returns the Use French note rather than deleting it.
[integration] After B's refile, refreshMemoryIndex on store A renders the user index line for lang without the (forget pending) marker.
[integration] When nothing changed lang after A recorded the forget, refreshMemoryIndex on store A renders the lang line with the (forget pending) marker.
[integration] (control) After B's refile, refreshMemoryIndex on store A leaves store A's readPendingForgets() unchanged.
[integration] (control) When userDir is null and the record holds a user-scope entry, refreshMemoryIndex resolves and writes the project index.

[integration] (control; failure handling) When readNote returns null or a note with status superseded, rejected or deleted at approval time, approveMemoryNote rejects with code MEMORY_NOTE_NOT_FOUND, as today, even when readPendingForgets is configured to throw if consulted; the revision check is never reached.
[integration] (control) When removing a stale entry throws, store A's readPendingForgets() retains that stale entry for the next approval.
[integration] When approval is retried after the stale-entry write failure is removed, it treats that entry as stale again and returns the replacement note with status active.
[integration] (control) When readNote throws while refreshMemoryIndex evaluates a recorded entry for a renderable note, the rendered line retains the (forget pending) marker, as today.

routing.reasoning: Two existing consumers adopt the upstream predicate inside established locking and index flows; the two-store production-entry regression is essential. Memory approval is a local state transition, not an authentication or access-control change.

userStories.title: Preserve current registry metadata and single-flight ACP reopens
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Preserve turn metadata across delayed model/mode switches and make overlapping load/resume requests reopen one session only once.

**Motivation** — A prompt completed while a model switch was waiting on `ensureCredentials`. The switch then wrote the entry's earlier metadata, which erased the title, `updatedAt` and the $0.25 `costUsd` that `recordTurn` had just persisted.

**Approach** — Implement these Target design requirements, not the baseline behavior:

- `switchTo` (`packages/nax-agent-acp/src/server/registry.ts`).
  - Target: after the switch succeeds, it reads `const current = entries.get(sessionId) ?? entry`. It then writes `meta = { ...current.meta, mode: next.mode, model: next.model, bashApproval: next.bashApproval }` into `entries.set(sessionId, { ...current, meta })` and `deps.storage.writeMeta(meta)`. A `title`, `updatedAt` or `costUsd` that `recordTurn` wrote during the `ensureCredentials` await is kept. The `?? entry` fallback is defensive only: a close requested during the switch makes `ServerSession.switchTo` throw `sessionClosed()` before this write (`server-session.ts`), so the write is never reached for a closed entry.
- `createReopen().reopen` (`packages/nax-agent-acp/src/server/registry-open.ts`).
  - Target: the reopener keeps a private `Map<string, Promise<void>>` of in-flight opens, keyed by session id. A reopen that finds no open entry and an in-flight open for its id awaits that promise, ignoring its rejection. It then re-runs `reopen(sessionId, input, replay)` from the top, which takes the already-open branch (a `load` waiter replays the stored transcript to the open entry's port, as an already-open `load` does today), or opens afresh if the first open failed. The first open sets the map entry before its first await (`storage.readMeta`) and deletes it in a `finally`. A waiter that re-runs after `closeAll` started is refused `SHUTTING_DOWN` by `openEntry`, as any open after shutdown is. `registry-open.ts` is 101 lines.

Read-only integration: `recordTurn(sessionId, prompt, costUsd)` writes `{ ...entry.meta, costUsd, title, updatedAt }` into entries and storage; `openEntry(meta, port, mcpServers)` ends with `entries.set(meta.sessionId, ...)`. Preserve their existing lifecycle, cleanup and entry shapes. Failure handling: The first of two overlapping reopens fails: The waiting reopen ignores that rejection and opens the session itself. Only the first caller sees the error.

Create registry-races.test.ts using registry-setup.ts rather than a parallel mock stack. For switch tests, let the create credential lookup resolve immediately, hold the second lookup, finish a `priced(0.25)` prompt while it is held, and then release it; assert persistence only after the switch resolves. Include the sequential control. For reopen tests, create and close the session in a first registry, create a second registry over the same sessions directory, gate openSession, and start two requests before releasing it. Check returned mode/model through SessionState.modes.currentModeId and the configOptions entry with id model and its currentValue, plus open count, closed() for every returned fake and release count after closeAll. These are existing response fields, not new top-level mode/model properties. Use existing failOpens/openGate and transcripts extras to cover first-open failure and two load replays. Use deferred promises to force the relevant interleaving and ensure cleanup releases gates even on failure.

**Scope** — In: post-switch current-entry metadata overlay, per-id in-flight coordination, waiter retry/replay semantics, race regressions and cleanup assertions. Out: memory revision and approval/index changes belong to US-001/US-002; cancelled-turn accounting belongs to US-004. US-003 only: a turn that starts after the switch's busy check and is still running when the switch resumes is not newly refused; the existing `ServerSession.switchTo` busy guard covers it. US-003 only: the in-flight reopen map is per registry instance; reopens of one session across separate server processes are coordinated by the file-backed session lock, as today.

**Interface** — Preserve the existing reopener contract and map value shape:
```typescript
reopen(sessionId: string, input: OpenInput, replay: boolean): Promise<SessionState>;
Map<string, Promise<void>>
```
Read-only integration calls: `recordTurn(sessionId, prompt, costUsd)` and `openEntry(meta, port, mcpServers)`. The successful switch writes exactly:
```typescript
const current = entries.get(sessionId) ?? entry;
const meta = { ...current.meta, mode: next.mode, model: next.model, bashApproval: next.bashApproval };
entries.set(sessionId, { ...current, meta });
await deps.storage.writeMeta(meta);
```
acceptanceCriteria: [integration] Given registry-setup.ts with ensureCredentials resolving immediately for create and held on its second call for a model setConfigOption switch, a new session with no prior turn (persisted title null and updatedAt null) completes a priced(0.25) prompt during the held lookup; after releasing the lookup and resolving the switch, storage.readMeta(sessionId).costUsd is 0.25.
[integration] In that delayed-switch case, storage.readMeta(sessionId).title equals the prompt's title rather than null.
[integration] In that delayed-switch case, storage.readMeta(sessionId).updatedAt is not null.
[integration] In that delayed-switch case, storage.readMeta(sessionId).model equals the newly selected model.
[integration] (control) With the priced turn finished before setConfigOption starts, persisted metadata has the new model.
[integration] (control) With the priced turn finished before setConfigOption starts, persisted metadata retains costUsd 0.25.
[integration] (control) With the priced turn finished before setConfigOption starts, persisted metadata retains the prompt's title.

[integration] Given a stored session created and shut down with closeAll on a first registry, when two resume(sessionId, input) calls overlap on a second registry over the same sessions directory while its openSession is held pending, the second registry calls openSession exactly once.

[integration] In that overlapping-resume case, both resume calls resolve with SessionState whose modes.currentModeId equals the stored mode and whose configOptions entry with id model has currentValue equal to the stored model.
[integration] In that overlapping-resume case, after closeAll on the second registry, closed() is true on every fake session its openSession returned.
[integration] In that overlapping-resume case, after closeAll on the second registry, releases() equals the number of fake sessions its openSession returned.

[integration] When the first of two overlapping resume calls on the second registry fails because openSession rejects once, the second resume resolves with the stored session's state, represented by modes.currentModeId and the model configOptions entry's currentValue.
[integration] When the first overlapping resume's openSession rejects once and the waiting resume succeeds, openSession has been called twice in total.
[integration] With a stored transcript seeded through the transcripts extra, two overlapping load(sessionId, input) calls on the second registry call openSession exactly once.
[integration] In that overlapping-load case, the shared fake port receives the transcript's replay twice, once per load call.
[integration] (control) A resume started on the second registry after an overlapping pair has settled finds the open entry and does not call openSession again.
[integration] (control) When the first overlapping reopen fails and its waiting caller subsequently succeeds, only the first caller receives the original openSession rejection.

routing.reasoning: Concurrent session lifecycle, lock-release ownership, transcript replay and credential-await interleavings span registry modules. Session/credential involvement requires strict three-session test isolation regardless of complexity.

suggestedCriteria: When closeAll starts while an overlapping reopen pair is waiting to open, the retrying waiter rejects with SHUTTING_DOWN instead of opening a session after shutdown.

userStories.title: Keep answered token usage when cancellation grace expires
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Preserve answered prompts' carried token usage on a cancelled denied-permission continuation that misses the cancellation grace.

**Motivation** — The first prompt reported 10 input and 5 output tokens. When the continuation answered within the grace period, the cancelled turn reported 12 and 6. When it missed the grace, the same turn reported 0 and 0, because the abort path attaches `NO_RESPONSE_SPEND` without the carried usage.

**Approach** — Implement this Target design requirement, not the baseline behavior:

- `promptOnce` abort branch (`packages/nax-agent-acp/src/client/turn.ts`).
  - Target: when `response` is undefined and `carried` is defined, it attaches `{ ...NO_RESPONSE_SPEND, tokenUsage: tokenUsageOf(carried) }`, the same shape the `failed` branch uses. When both are undefined, it attaches `NO_RESPONSE_SPEND`. Cost stays `0` / `unpriced` because the cumulative cost meter carries the reading to the next turn.

Read `runPromptTurn`, `cancelTurn` and the existing failure path before changing the abort path. Reuse `sumUsage(first, second)` and `tokenUsageOf(usage)` from usage.ts unchanged. A response inside grace continues to settle the collector using sumUsage over carried and response usage; a no-response abort must not newly settle the cost meter. Keep the current thrown abort reason, cancellation classification, disconnect behavior and kill ownership.

Add missed-grace regressions to `test/unit/client/backend-codex.test.ts`, reusing its denied-then-cancelled peer fixture and driveTurn instead of copying them, per the project rule against copy-pasted mock setup. Its local OpenOptions and open() gain an optional cancelGraceMs passed through to the backend options. No existing assertion changes. Use a read-only profile with cancelGraceMs 50. The first prompt requests permission, is denied by the read-only policy, and returns cancelled with 10 input and 5 output tokens; after DENIED_CONTINUATION_PROMPT reaches the peer, have its continuation hang and invoke AgentSession.cancel(). Observe the production terminal turn_end event for carried tokens, cancelled status and zero/unpriced cost, and observe exactly one process kill before teardown. Also exercise a continuation that answers inside grace with 2 input and 1 output tokens, and the first-prompt/no-carried-usage hang control. The existing backend.test.ts kill-after-grace test is context, not a new copied fixture.

**Scope** — In: carried token spend attachment in the no-response abort branch, configurable grace in the existing test helper, and backend-level regressions. Out: memory changes belong to US-001/US-002; registry metadata and reopen coordination belong to US-003. US-004 only: the dollar cost of a turn that misses the cancellation grace is not attached to that turn; the cumulative ACP cost meter reports it on the next turn, as today.

**Interface** — Read-only existing helpers: `sumUsage(first, second)` and `tokenUsageOf(usage)`. The attached spend for an unanswered continuation is exactly:
```typescript
{ ...NO_RESPONSE_SPEND, tokenUsage: tokenUsageOf(carried) }
```
The no-carried/no-response case still attaches `NO_RESPONSE_SPEND`; no public API or event shape changes.
acceptanceCriteria: [integration] Through the ACP backend and backend-codex.test.ts scripted peer, with a read-only profile and cancelGraceMs 50, the first prompt is denied permission and answers cancelled with 10 input and 5 output tokens; when the peer hangs on DENIED_CONTINUATION_PROMPT and AgentSession.cancel() is called after the peer receives it, terminal turn_end.usage reports inputTokens 10 and outputTokens 5.
[integration] In that missed-grace continuation case, the agent process receives exactly one kill request.
[integration] In that missed-grace continuation case, terminal turn_end has status cancelled.
[integration] When that continuation instead answers inside the cancellation grace with 2 input and 1 output tokens, terminal turn_end.usage reports inputTokens 12 and outputTokens 6.
[integration] (control) When a first prompt with no carried usage hangs and the grace expires after AgentSession.cancel(), terminal turn_end.usage reports inputTokens 0 and outputTokens 0.
[integration] In the missed-grace continuation case, terminal turn_end reports costUsd 0 and costSource unpriced.

routing.reasoning: A narrow existing spend-attachment change plus test-option plumbing, but session cancellation and denied-permission paths trigger the mandatory strict three-session isolation override.

modifiedFiles.reason: the new missed-grace tests are added here, reusing its denied-then-cancelled peer fixture and `driveTurn` instead of copying them, per the project rule against copy-pasted mock setup. Its local `OpenOptions` and `open()` gain an optional `cancelGraceMs` passed through to the backend options. No existing assertion changes.

analysis:
Existing-code bug-fix feature, not greenfield. Implement exactly four stories: US-001 and US-002 in packages/nax-agent, with US-002 depending on US-001; US-003 and US-004 independently in packages/nax-agent-acp. Codebase-memory MCP is unavailable in this host, so discovery used direct reads and text searches rooted at the supplied execution repository. No production code or tests were changed or executed while drafting this PRD.

Memory model and persistence: packages/nax-agent/src/memory/types.ts:23 defines MemoryNote, including its id, updatedAt and status; types.ts:50 defines the currently four-field MemoryPendingForget. packages/nax-agent/src/memory/records.ts:36 defines PendingForgetSchema, and records.ts:75 parses pending-forget JSONL through that schema. Merely adding a TypeScript property is insufficient: the schema must retain noteId during readback. Add an optional string without changing validation of clientId, scope, slug or reason; legacy lines must retain the absent-field shape. packages/nax-agent/src/memory/store.ts:127 exposes MemoryStore, including readNote and record read/write operations. The store already handles confined file I/O, JSONL persistence and path/scope refusal; its contract is read-only for this feature. Keep its existing path validation and record-error behavior intact.

US-001 change sites: packages/nax-agent/src/memory/local-provider.ts:74 constructs queuedForget without a revision; local-provider.ts:79 compares only the four existing fields; local-provider.ts:99 filters by memoryNoteKey and skips unchanged rewrites. The provider at local-provider.ts:108 handles saves and forgets. A proposal forget must best-effort read the held note before rewriting its record, append noteId only for a non-null successful read, and compare noteId when detecting a changed record. Catch only the added note lookup for fallback: record read/write failures must still propagate through the existing throughStore classification. Direct forget behavior and save-time record clearing remain unchanged. Do not assume every proposal target exists: the provider can accept a proposal for a missing user directory or missing note, even though the higher-level forget operation normally requires a held note. Create forget-revision.ts as a small module exporting isStaleForget; this is a module export consumed inside memory, not a request to expand the supported package root export list. packages/nax-agent/src/memory/index.ts:1 and packages/nax-agent/src/index.ts:114 already expose the existing memory API, including MemoryPendingForget. The optional field is an additive type change; no new public barrel name is required.

US-002 revision identity and locking: packages/nax-agent/src/memory/operations.ts:134 mints randomUUID() in stagedNote on every save, while operations.ts:332 changes status and updatedAt in inForce without changing id. Therefore id, not timestamp, distinguishes a refile from approval of the same pending revision. operations.ts:362 reads the note and refuses absent/retired statuses before checking the record; operations.ts:374 currently returns only a boolean for a matching key. Change that decision path to inspect the matching entry and distinguish stale from current. Current entries continue to operations.ts:388 retireRecorded, whose delete-then-reread/filter/write/refresh sequence preserves its failure contract and other keys. Stale entries must instead be removed without deleting the note, using a fresh record read for removal so other writers' entries are retained, followed by refreshIndex even for an already-active note. Only then continue normal approval: active notes retain their timestamp; pending notes activate with the approval clock and keep their id. All of this remains inside the existing orderedByMirrorLocks plus withMirrorLock wrapper at operations.ts:423. The module is already 425 lines; locate the shared revision predicate in the new helper rather than growing another independent rule here.

Index integration: packages/nax-agent/src/memory/index-render.ts:205 currently unions all recorded keys with caller-held keys and source keys, and index-render.ts:225 regenerates the scope indexes. Filter only recorded keys through isStaleForget against readNote; any lookup exception keeps the recorded marker, and rendering never rewrites pending-forgets.jsonl. Held/source keys still mark independently, even when a stale recorded entry has the same key. The user MEMORY.md is written to the shared user directory, not embedded in the project index; inspect the user index for user/lang assertions. Preserve the userDir:null project-only path. packages/nax/src/cli/memory-write.ts:234-238 already chooses the correct messages from returned status and remains untouched.

Memory regression harnesses: packages/nax-agent/test/unit/memory/local-provider-pending-forgets.test.ts exercises real stores, provider pushes, exact entry shapes, no-op record writes, save clearing, invalid slug rejection and propagated I/O failures. Update an exact-shape assertion only when its forgotten key actually has a held note; absent-target assertions must remain four-field entries. packages/nax-agent/test/unit/memory/store-pending-forgets.test.ts exercises ordered JSONL round trips, legacy records, skipped malformed lines and confinement; extend its round trip for entries with and without noteId. packages/nax-agent/test/unit/memory/operations-approve-forget.test.ts:320 has the single-store endToEnd harness to extend conceptually into a two-store fixture in the new stale-forget test file. Use separate projectDir values and one shared userDir; each project must have its own provider/outbox/logger so B cannot accidentally clear A's record.
